clinician.final_diagnosis: Lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old female presented in September 2014 with nephrotic syndrome (heavy proteinuria 2.7 g/day, severe hypoalbuminemia 17.2 g/L, edema, ascites), active urinary sediment (dysmorphic RBCs, granular casts), and renal dysfunction (creatinine 167.3 μmol/l, eGFR 42 ml/min/1.73m²). Serologic workup revealed strongly positive ANA (homogeneous pattern), elevated anti-dsDNA (30 IU/ml), leukopenia (1.7 × 10⁹/L), and anemia (18%), consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus. Renal biopsy (E005) demonstrated marked mesangial cell increase without GBM thickening/duplication, consistent with ISN/RPS Class II lupus nephritis, with superimposed acute tubular necrosis features. During admission, she became oliguric and uremic requiring dialysis (E007). In the third week, she developed hyperpigmented malar rash, gum hypertrophy, and bleeding (E006), confirming cutaneous lupus involvement. She received intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g daily × 3 days) followed by oral prednisolone taper and mycophenolate mofetil 720 mg twice daily. After 6 months of treatment, she demonstrated significant clinical response with proteinuria reduction to 0.2 g/day, serum creatinine improvement to 94 μmol/l, eGFR recovery to 82 ml/min/1.73m², and ESR decrease to 44 mm/hr (E007).
